title: How Two Generals Led Sudan to the Brink of Civil War

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店做DJ时，你每晚也要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，然后你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重塑者》吧。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Over the past week in Sudan, a closely-watched plan to create a democracy has instead turned into a deadly civil war.
sentences.zh: 过去一周，苏丹一项备受瞩目的民主化计划演变成了一场致命的内战。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Declan Walsh, on the personal rivalry at the center of the conflict.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事德克兰·沃尔什将讲述这场冲突核心的个人恩怨。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月24日，星期一。

sentences.en: So Declan, describe the scene in Sudan's capital over the past few days.
sentences.zh: 德克兰，请描述一下过去几天苏丹首都的情况。

sentences.en: Well, Michael, it started for me with a text message.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，对我来说，这一切始于一条短信。

sentences.en: It was last Saturday morning.
sentences.zh: 那是上周六早上。

sentences.en: I was at home.
sentences.zh: 我当时在家。

sentences.en: I got a message from a friend of mine in Khartoum, which is the capital of Sudan.
sentences.zh: 我收到了一位住在苏丹首都喀土穆的朋友发来的消息。

sentences.en: And the message said, war has just erupted in Khartoum.
sentences.zh: 消息说，喀土穆刚刚爆发了战争。

sentences.en: And then he went on to explain that his house is about 400 meters from a military camp in the city that had come under attack.
sentences.zh: 他接着解释说，他的房子距离城里一个遭到袭击的军营大约400米。

sentences.en: And he sent me a clip of a recording he'd made out the window of his house.
sentences.zh: 他给我发了一段他从自家窗户录下的视频。

sentences.en: And the clip went thud, thud, thud, thud with gunfire.
sentences.zh: 视频里传来砰、砰、砰、砰的枪声。

sentences.en: And I guess that was the starting gun for what has become this crazy descent into violence that has consumed the capital of Sudan and spread across the entire country.
sentences.zh: 我想那就是这场疯狂暴力冲突的开端，它吞噬了苏丹首都，并蔓延到了全国各地。

sentences.en: Within the hours that followed that, everything moves incredibly quickly.
sentences.zh: 在那之后的几个小时里，一切发展得极快。

sentences.en: There is fighting around the presidential palace, the headquarters of the military.
sentences.zh: 总统府和军方总部周围发生了战斗。

sentences.en: At the international airport, passengers are taking cover on the ground of the terminal because there's fighting and bombs outside.
sentences.zh: 在国际机场，乘客们趴在航站楼的地板上躲避，因为外面正在交火，还有炸弹爆炸。

sentences.en: You get warplanes that start whizzing over the city, firing rockets and dropping bombs.
sentences.zh: 战机开始在城市上空呼啸而过，发射火箭弹并投下炸弹。

sentences.en: And you get these small street-to-street battles flaring everywhere in residential neighborhoods, on the main bridges that cross the Nile and the city, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在居民区、横跨尼罗河和城市的主要桥梁上，到处都爆发了小规模的巷战。

sentences.en: And over the last week, this tempo has continued.
sentences.zh: 过去一周，这种节奏一直持续着。

sentences.en: We have been hearing very loud gunfire and shootings all over the city of Khartoum.
sentences.zh: 我们一直听到喀土穆全城传来非常响亮的枪声和射击声。

sentences.en: And in the middle of it, you've got millions of citizens who've been trapped in their homes, cowering against this violence.
sentences.zh: 而在这一切之中，数百万市民被困在家中，在暴力威胁下瑟瑟发抖。

sentences.en: Now we stay without electricity, without water, without bread, without anything.
sentences.zh: 现在我们没有电，没有水，没有面包，什么都没有。

sentences.en: So we need somebody to help us, please.
sentences.zh: 所以请找人帮帮我们。

sentences.en: Slowly running out of food and water.
sentences.zh: 食物和水快用完了。

sentences.en: Now we are imprisoned in Khartoum, in this situation.
sentences.zh: 现在我们被困在喀土穆，处境艰难。

sentences.en: And in recent days, trying to figure out whether they should be trying to escape the city.
sentences.zh: 最近几天，人们一直在纠结是否应该尝试逃离这座城市。

sentences.en: And at the heart of this conflict are two figures.
sentences.zh: 这场冲突的核心是两个人物。

sentences.en: There's the army chief,
sentences.zh: 一位是陆军参谋长，

sentences.en: General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and a man called Lieutenant General Mohammed Hamdan, better known by everybody as Hemeti, who heads this much smaller,
sentences.zh: 阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·布尔汉将军，另一位是穆罕默德·哈姆丹中将，大家更熟悉的名字是“赫梅蒂”，他领导着这支规模小得多，
zh_words: 阿卜杜勒·法塔赫·布尔汉

sentences.en: but very powerful paramilitary group called the Rapid Support Forces.
sentences.zh: 但非常强大的准军事组织，名为“快速支援部队”。

sentences.en: Now, these two groups are two branches of Sudan's military.
sentences.zh: 这两个组织实际上是苏丹军队的两个分支。

sentences.en: And all the fighting that's taking place is between soldiers of these two rival units of the same military.
sentences.zh: 所有的战斗都是在这支军队中两个敌对单位的士兵之间进行的。

sentences.en: So this is essentially a civil war within Sudan's military that is playing out in a very painful way across the capital city, which sounds absolutely terrifying.
sentences.zh: 所以这本质上是苏丹军队内部的一场内战，正在首都以一种极其痛苦的方式上演，听起来绝对令人恐惧。

sentences.en: I'm trying to think of the equivalent in a place like the U.S., and all I can imagine is something like the army going to war with the Marines in Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 我试着想一下在美国类似的情况，我只能想象陆军和海军陆战队在华盛顿特区开战，

sentences.en: and that would be nightmarishly awful.
sentences.zh: 那将是噩梦般的可怕。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's just as bad as that.
sentences.zh: 情况就是那么糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, the great tragedy of it, Michael, is that, you know, this was the moment when Sudan was supposed to be moving away from military rule, and instead the country finds itself
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，迈克尔，最悲剧的是，你知道，这本应是苏丹摆脱军事统治的时刻，但国家却发现自己

sentences.en: in what everybody feared was this nightmare scenario tumbling into a civil war.
sentences.zh: 陷入了每个人都担心的噩梦场景，坠入了内战。

sentences.en: So how did we get to this nightmarish place, and how do these two generals fit into that story?
sentences.zh: 那么我们是如何走到这个噩梦般的境地的？这两位将军在故事中扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, to understand that story and how these generals fit into it, you've got to go back to 2019.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，要理解这个故事以及这两位将军在其中的角色，你必须回到2019年。

sentences.en: That was when tens of thousands of Sudanese massed at the gates of the country's military headquarters and eventually forced the ouster of the country's ruler of 30 years,
sentences.zh: 当时成千上万的苏丹人聚集在国家军事总部大门前，最终迫使统治了该国30年的领导人下台，

sentences.en: Omar Hassan al-Bashir.
sentences.zh: 即奥马尔·哈桑·巴希尔。

sentences.en: Women started to have more rights because the hated morality police was disbanded.
sentences.zh: 女性开始拥有更多权利，因为令人憎恶的道德警察被解散了。

sentences.en: Artists were making revolutionary art.
sentences.zh: 艺术家们创作着革命艺术。

sentences.en: There was a whole new political movement that sprang up.
sentences.zh: 一场全新的政治运动应运而生。

sentences.en: You know, it was this euphoric moment where millions of Sudanese thought that after decades of isolation, they were going to turn a corner.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是一个令人陶醉的时刻，数百万苏丹人认为，在经历了数十年的孤立后，他们终于要迎来转机了。

sentences.en: And the extraordinary thing is that these two generals,
sentences.zh: 非同寻常的是，这两位将军，

sentences.en: General Burhan and General Hamdan, also known as Hemeti, up to this point, they're among President Bashir's closest henchmen.
sentences.zh: 布尔汉将军和哈姆丹将军（即赫梅蒂），在这一刻之前，他们还是巴希尔总统最亲近的爪牙。

sentences.en: And then at the moment of the revolution, they turn on him.
sentences.zh: 然后在革命的关键时刻，他们背叛了他。

sentences.en: They help to kick him out from office.
sentences.zh: 他们帮助将他赶下了台。

sentences.en: And then as the country moves through this period of dramatic change, they're at the heart of it.
sentences.zh: 随着国家经历这一剧烈变革时期，他们处于核心地位。

sentences.en: They say that they want to be part of a new Sudan, and they say that they're going to help to shepherd the country towards free and fair elections.
sentences.zh: 他们声称自己想成为新苏丹的一部分，并表示将帮助引导国家走向自由公正的选举。

sentences.en: And what exactly is the role of these two generals in this transition from autocracy to what is supposed to become a democracy?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这场从独裁向民主过渡的过程中，这两位将军究竟扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Well, they're both members of something called the Sovereignty Council, which is this body with civilian and military leaders that was supposed to be overseeing the country
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们都是“主权委员会”的成员，这是一个由文职和军事领导人组成的机构，本应负责监督国家

sentences.en: during the transition to democracy.
sentences.zh: 在向民主过渡期间的运作。

sentences.en: Burhan was the senior guy.
sentences.zh: 布尔汉是资历较深的那位。

sentences.en: He's the head of the military, which is this institution that has dominated Sudan and personally, he's this decorated elite general.
sentences.zh: 他是军队的首脑，这支机构长期统治着苏丹，他本人是一位获得过勋章的精英将军。

sentences.en: He's often seen pictured with a row of medals and a stiff bearing.
sentences.zh: 人们经常看到他佩戴着一排勋章，举止严谨。

sentences.en: And then you've got Hemity, who's this kind of like upstart figure.
sentences.zh: 然后是赫梅蒂，他算是一个暴发户式的人物。

sentences.en: He established himself by running a militia, which was known for its scorched earth tactics during the genocide in Darfur in the 2000s.
sentences.zh: 他通过经营一支民兵组织确立了自己的地位，该组织因2000年代达尔富尔种族灭绝期间的焦土政策而闻名。

sentences.en: That militia eventually morphed into the Rapid Support Forces, or ORSF for short, which is the paramilitary group he heads now.
sentences.zh: 那支民兵组织最终演变成了“快速支援部队”（简称RSF），也就是他现在领导的准军事组织。

sentences.en: And through the ORSF, he has really risen through the ranks of power in Sudan, amassing huge amounts of both wealth and influence.
sentences.zh: 通过RSF，他在苏丹的权力阶层中迅速崛起，积累了巨大的财富和影响力。

sentences.en: So on this council,
sentences.zh: 所以在这个委员会里，

sentences.en: General Burhan, in his position as head of the military, acts as the chairman and effectively the head of state during this transitional period.
sentences.zh: 布尔汉将军作为军队首脑，担任主席，实际上是过渡时期的国家元首。

sentences.en: And Hemity, who is also a member of the Sovereignty Council, is considered to be the second most powerful person in Sudan.
sentences.zh: 而同样是主权委员会成员的赫梅蒂，被认为是苏丹第二大权力人物。

sentences.en: So somewhat improbably, both of these generals, despite being originally associated with this autocrat who so many people in Sudan rebelled against, it is these two generals
sentences.zh: 所以有些不可思议的是，这两位将军，尽管最初与许多苏丹人反抗的独裁者有关联，但最终却是他们两人

sentences.en: who end up being entrusted with a transition to democracy.
sentences.zh: 被委以民主过渡的重任。

sentences.en: So how does that go?
sentences.zh: 那么进展如何呢？

sentences.en: Well, for a little while, it seems to be going pretty well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一段时间，看起来进展得相当顺利。

sentences.en: You've got consultants flying in.
sentences.zh: 有顾问飞抵这里。

sentences.en: You've got a lot of people who are saying they want to help this transition go along.
sentences.zh: 很多人都说他们想帮助这次过渡顺利进行。

sentences.en: And the revolution in Sudan brings in a lot of Western and regional countries who say that they also want it to succeed.
sentences.zh: 苏丹的革命吸引了许多西方和地区国家，他们也表示希望革命成功。

sentences.en: So they send billions of dollars in aid.
sentences.zh: 于是他们提供了数十亿美元的援助。

sentences.en: There's like up to $50 billion in debt relief that is promised to Sudan.
sentences.zh: 承诺给苏丹的债务减免高达500亿美元。

sentences.en: And why was that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: I mean, why was this transition so important to these outside countries, especially in the West?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么这次过渡对这些外部国家，尤其是西方国家如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, for several reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，原因有几个。

sentences.en: Sudan is the third largest country in Africa.
sentences.zh: 苏丹是非洲第三大国家。

sentences.en: It had been isolated for decades under the former dictator, al-Bashir, and particularly by the United States, which had placed the country under sanctions.
sentences.zh: 在前独裁者巴希尔的统治下，它被孤立了数十年，特别是受到美国的制裁。

sentences.en: So I think that for the U.S., they wanted to turn a page, a new chapter with Sudan.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为美国想翻开新的一页，开启与苏丹关系的新篇章。

sentences.en: But more broadly, this is this huge country.
sentences.zh: 但更广泛地说，这是一个巨大的国家。

sentences.en: It's very strategically located on the Red Sea.
sentences.zh: 它在红海的战略位置非常重要。

sentences.en: And frankly, for Western countries, at this point, they're seeing other strategic competitors in Africa.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，对于西方国家来说，他们现在看到了非洲的其他战略竞争对手。

sentences.en: The Chinese are moving across the continent.
sentences.zh: 中国正在非洲大陆扩张。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Russians are starting to establish themselves.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯也开始建立自己的势力。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of countries wanted to make sure that in this very fragile moment of transition for Sudan, that they were the ones
sentences.zh: 我认为许多国家都想确保在苏丹这个极其脆弱的过渡时刻，他们是

sentences.en: who were going to be influencing how it would end.
sentences.zh: 能够影响最终结果的一方。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We've talked a lot about this on the show, especially when it comes to an adversary like China.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中经常讨论这个问题，特别是在涉及像中国这样的竞争对手时。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: wants to make sure that its influence is greatest on some of these African countries.
sentences.zh: 希望确保其在这些非洲国家的影响力最大。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而美国

sentences.en: is selling in Africa often is democracy.
sentences.zh: 在非洲兜售的往往是民主。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what happens next in this journey of these two generals towards what is supposed to be a democracy?
sentences.zh: 那么，这两位将军在通往所谓民主的旅程中，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: First of all, we've got to realise that it's not easy.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们必须意识到这并不容易。

sentences.en: Sudan, after 30 years under Bashir, is basically a broken country.
sentences.zh: 苏丹在巴希尔统治30年后，基本上是一个破碎的国家。

sentences.en: And it's got this very sort of underdeveloped, fractious political system.
sentences.zh: 它有着非常不发达、派系林立的政治体制。

sentences.en: So the civilians in the military really struggle to run the country together.
sentences.zh: 所以文职人员和军方在共同治理国家时确实很吃力。

sentences.en: The civilians are demanding accountability for prior abuses under the military, including a massacre of pro-democracy demonstrators, which had taken place just after the revolution
sentences.zh: 文职人员要求追究军方过去滥用职权的责任，包括革命后不久发生的一场针对亲民主示威者的屠杀，

sentences.en: and was blamed on both
sentences.zh: 而这被归咎于

sentences.en: General Hematy and General Burhan.
sentences.zh: 赫梅蒂将军和布尔汉将军两人。

sentences.en: And that starts to ratchet up the tension between these two sides.
sentences.zh: 这开始加剧双方之间的紧张关系。

sentences.en: Those tensions build and build.
sentences.zh: 这些紧张局势不断升级。

sentences.en: And after about two years in October 2021, these two generals,
sentences.zh: 大约两年后的2021年10月，这两位将军，

sentences.en: General Burhan and Hematy, come together secretly and they mount a coup and seize power for themselves, pushing aside the country's civilian prime minister.
sentences.zh: 布尔汉和赫梅蒂，秘密联手发动政变，夺取了权力，排挤了国家的文职总理。

sentences.en: They put him under house arrest and eventually, actually, he ends up leaving the country.
sentences.zh: 他们将他软禁起来，最终他实际上离开了这个国家。

sentences.en: So these generals are completely reneging on their pledge to bring Sudan into democracy.
sentences.zh: 所以这些将军完全违背了他们将苏丹带向民主的承诺。

sentences.en: In fact, they are blocking that journey to democracy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们正在阻碍通往民主的道路。

sentences.en: So what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, straight away, protesters flood back on the streets, determined that the dream of democracy that seemed to be so close, they're not going to let go of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，抗议者立刻涌回街头，他们决心不放弃那个看起来触手可及的民主梦想。

sentences.en: The economy starts tanking because the West pulls the dollars that it promised as punishment for the coup.
sentences.zh: 经济开始下滑，因为西方为了惩罚政变，撤回了承诺的资金。

sentences.en: And then slowly, slowly, behind closed doors, cracks start to form between these two generals themselves.
sentences.zh: 然后慢慢地，在幕后，这两位将军之间开始出现裂痕。

sentences.en: And eventually, they turn on each other.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们反目成仇。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们每年可能都是联盟中最好的球队。
